units.title: Unit 73 — Complaining and protesting
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition); printed pages 152–153 (PDF pages 154–155).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition)
units.category: Communicative functions · complaints, protests and register
learningObjectives: Choose appropriate language for informal, neutral and formal complaints.
Use protest, complain, object and remonstrate with their correct complements and prepositions.
Distinguish grumble, gripe, grouse and whinge by tone and register.
Interpret indirect criticism and tactful complaints.

sectionsChecked: B · Verbs and nouns relating to complaining and protesting

items.pt: tomar providências a respeito; fazer algo para resolver
items.example: The neighbours have complained repeatedly, so the landlord must do something about it.
items.note: Directly demands action; usually informal and can sound forceful.

items.example: For goodness’ sake, stop interrupting the speaker and let her finish.
items.note: An informal exclamation showing irritation or impatience; tone matters.

items.pt: de saco cheio; farto; cansado de uma situação
items.example: The residents are fed up with the constant disruption caused by building work.
items.note: Use fed up with a noun or an -ing form; an informal complaint.

items.pt: de saco cheio disso; farto disso
items.example: I have explained the same problem four times, and I'm sick of it.
items.note: An informal, emphatic way to express that you can no longer tolerate something.

items.pt: reclamar sem parar; ficar resmungando sobre
items.example: He keeps moaning about minor inconveniences rather than offering solutions.
items.note: Often suggests excessive or unproductive complaining; generally disapproving.

items.example: Look here, we agreed on a deadline and you have missed it twice.
items.note: An emphatic opening to a complaint; can sound confrontational or old-fashioned.

items.pt: estou quase no meu limite; já estou praticamente farto disso
items.example: I have just about had enough of the repeated changes to my schedule.
items.note: Strong informal warning that one’s patience is nearly exhausted.

items.example: Charging guests for a service they never received is simply not on.
items.note: Chiefly British informal English for behaviour judged unacceptable; often used as it is not on.

items.example: After months of avoidable delays, the committee finally said enough is enough.
items.note: A forceful declaration that an unacceptable situation must stop.

items.example: His grumbling about the new policy made the atmosphere unnecessarily tense.
items.note: Repeated low-level complaints; often heard as a negative attitude.

items.example: We are not at all satisfied with the quality of the revised report.
items.note: A clear but relatively neutral expression of dissatisfaction; commonly with.

items.pt: algo precisa ser feito; providências precisam ser tomadas
items.example: Something must be done about the unsafe pedestrian crossing before an accident occurs.
items.note: A relatively impersonal complaint that focuses on the need for action.

items.pt: eu gostaria que você fizesse; queria que você
items.example: I wish you would consult the team before changing the project schedule.
items.note: Wish + would often communicates dissatisfaction with behaviour one wants changed.

items.pt: gostaria que você parasse de; queria que você não
items.example: I wish you wouldn’t leave confidential papers on the reception desk.
items.note: Wish + would not criticises a recurring action; a polite delivery can soften it.

items.pt: assim não dá; isso não é aceitável
items.example: Consistently ignoring the safety procedure just won’t do.
items.note: An idiomatic, firm statement that behaviour or performance is unacceptable.

items.pt: mudar de comportamento; mudar seus hábitos
items.example: The manager told him to change his ways if he wanted to keep his position.
items.note: Suggests changing repeated bad habits rather than fixing one isolated error.

items.pt: desejar registrar uma reclamação; querer reclamar formalmente
items.example: I wish to complain about the unexplained charges on my latest statement.
items.note: Formal opening for a written or official complaint; typically followed by about.

items.example: The absence of an independent review is most unsatisfactory.
items.note: Most functions as a formal intensifier, not a superlative comparison here.

items.example: Several researchers took exception to the inaccurate account of their findings.
items.note: A strong formal expression of objection; to is a preposition, so an -ing form may follow.

items.word: I must object to the proposal
items.pt: precisar se opor a; ter de contestar
items.example: I really must object to being excluded from a decision that affects my work.
items.note: Formal, emphatic dissent; object to is followed by a noun, pronoun or -ing form.

items.example: Leaving residents without clean water for several days is simply unacceptable.
items.note: Strong formal assessment that conduct or a situation falls below acceptable standards.

items.example: The deliberate destruction of the documents was a shameful abuse of power.
items.note: Strong moral criticism, implying that the responsible party should feel ashamed.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: Passengers complained about the repeated cancellations at the regional airport.
items.note: Complain about something; complain to someone when naming the recipient.

items.pt: fazer uma reclamação a; queixar-se para
items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: She complained to the head of department about the biased assessment.
items.note: The recipient follows to; the problem usually follows about.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: Local businesses protested about the sudden increase in commercial rents.
items.note: The verb is stressed on the second syllable; protest may be followed by about or against.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: The students organised a peaceful protest outside the council offices.
items.note: The noun typically has first-syllable stress, unlike the verb protest.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: Many employees object to having their personal data shared without consent.
items.note: To is a preposition: object to a noun or to doing something, not to do.

items.pt: repreender ou protestar junto a alguém; argumentar contra
items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: The chair remonstrated with the organisers over the lack of accessible seating.
items.note: Very formal: remonstrate with a person; remonstrate about or against a matter.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: Some reviewers find fault with every stylistic choice the author makes.
items.note: Often implies focusing on even minor shortcomings rather than balanced criticism.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: The technicians grumbled about the frequent last-minute changes.
items.note: A relatively quiet, often resentful kind of complaint.

items.pt: reclamar continuamente de; ficar se queixando de
items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: Staff kept griping about the lack of proper equipment.
items.note: Informal and often suggests persistent complaint.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: He spent the journey grousing about the cost of accommodation.
items.note: Informal; often implies repetitive and somewhat petty dissatisfaction.

items.section: B · Verbs for complaint and protest
items.example: They spent most of the meeting whingeing about the new timetable.
items.note: Chiefly British informal usage; usually disapproving of prolonged, irritating complaints.

items.example: The regulator received a formal complaint about misleading advertisements.
items.note: The noun form of complain; a complaint about an issue can be made to an authority.

items.example: The committee raised an objection to the proposed amendment.
items.note: Often followed by to; raise or lodge an objection are established collocations.

items.example: The board received a formal remonstrance concerning the new restrictions.
items.note: An uncommon, highly formal noun related to remonstrate.

items.pt: atitude de criticar ou apontar defeitos constantemente
items.example: Constant fault-finding discouraged younger colleagues from offering suggestions.
items.note: Often negatively evaluates habitual, excessively critical behaviour.

items.example: One recurring gripe among employees concerns the unreliable booking system.
items.note: Informal countable noun; distinct from the verb gripe.

items.example: His main grouse was that nobody had consulted him beforehand.
items.note: Informal countable noun for something someone repeatedly complains about.

items.example: The editor dismissed the article as little more than a whinge.
items.note: Chiefly British informal noun with a dismissive tone.

items.example: You would be well advised to check the contract before signing it.
items.note: Polite or indirect warning; often implies potential consequences if advice is ignored.

items.pt: uma demão de tinta; uma pintura rápida
items.example: The waiting room would benefit from a lick of paint and better lighting.
items.note: Informal phrase suggesting a small amount of redecoration.

items.example: His report tends to overlook the costs of maintaining the equipment.
items.note: In evaluations, tends to can soften a criticism while implying a recurring pattern.

items.pt: não ser uma prioridade; ficar em segundo plano
items.example: The appraisal implied that punctuality was not a high priority for the employee.
items.note: An indirect criticism whose apparently neutral wording may imply a recurring problem.

items.pt: poderia tomar alguma providência a respeito
items.example: I wish the local council could do something about it before winter.
items.note: Could softens the directive compared with you must do something.

units.title: Unit 74 — Apology, regret and reconciliation
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition); printed pages 154–155 (PDF pages 156–157).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition)
units.category: Communicative functions · apology, legal redress and peace agreements
learningObjectives: Choose precise collocations for apologies, explanations, excuses, alibis and pretexts.
Distinguish remorse, repentance, acquittal, exoneration, pardons and reprieves.
Use legal and apology patterns with accurate prepositions.
Compare a peace treaty, armistice, truce, accord and ceasefire.

items.example: She offered a sincere apology for revealing the information without permission.
items.note: A standard collocation emphasising genuine regret.

items.pt: um pedido de desculpas de coração; profundamente sincero
items.example: The director issued a heartfelt apology to families affected by the mistake.
items.note: More emotionally emphatic than sincere apology; heartfelt is not usually applied to an alibi.

items.pt: pedir desculpas; apresentar um pedido de desculpas
items.example: The company eventually offered an apology for the distress caused by its error.
items.note: More formal than simply saying sorry; can be qualified as sincere or heartfelt.

items.pt: uma justificativa plausível; uma boa desculpa
items.example: A medical emergency would be a good excuse for missing the deadline.
items.note: A reason that may reasonably justify an action.

items.pt: uma desculpa perfeita; uma justificativa ideal
items.example: The sudden transport strike gave him a perfect excuse to postpone the meeting.
items.note: Can indicate a genuinely excellent reason or a convenient pretext, depending on context.

items.example: Saying that he had forgotten the date was a lame excuse for missing the hearing.
items.note: An unconvincing, weak excuse, usually criticised by the speaker.

items.pt: uma desculpa pouco convincente; justificativa sem fundamento
items.example: The claim that nobody had read the policy seemed a flimsy excuse for ignoring it.
items.note: Weak and lacking convincing support; also combines with pretext.

items.pt: uma desculpa fraca; justificativa pouco convincente
items.example: The committee rejected his weak excuse for failing to disclose the conflict of interest.
items.note: A straightforward judgement that an excuse is insufficient.

items.example: The analyst gave a convincing explanation of the sudden change in demand.
items.note: A credible account; unlike an excuse, it need not justify wrongdoing.

items.example: The witness provided a detailed explanation of what happened before the alarm sounded.
items.note: Emphasises completeness and specifics, not necessarily truthfulness.

items.pt: uma explicação falsa; uma história inventada
items.example: Investigators suspected the supplier had given them a phoney explanation for the missing funds.
items.note: Phoney means false or not genuine; informal spelling used in British English.

items.pt: um álibi incontestável; álibi muito sólido
items.example: The footage provided her with a cast-iron alibi for the time of the burglary.
items.note: An exceptionally strong and convincing alibi, leaving little room for doubt.

items.example: The prosecutor alleged that the suspect had arranged a phoney alibi.
items.note: An alibi that is invented or deliberately misleading.

items.pt: um pretexto falso; uma justificativa inventada
items.example: The officials entered the building under a false pretext.
items.note: A stated reason designed to hide the real motive.

items.pt: um pretexto pouco crível; uma justificativa frágil
items.example: He contacted the researcher on the flimsy pretext of requesting an old article.
items.note: A weakly supported pretended reason; the usual phrase is on the pretext of.

items.example: They postponed the vote on the pretext of needing more time to review the evidence.
items.note: Often implies that the stated reason hides the speaker’s actual purpose.

items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The defendant showed genuine remorse for the harm he had caused.
items.note: A feeling of deep regret and guilt, not the same as a formal apology.

items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The court observed that the offender had shown no remorse during the proceedings.
items.note: Common legal collocation referring to the absence of regret.

items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The jury acquitted the accountant of fraud after examining the new evidence.
items.note: The passive form shows the accused was found not guilty; use acquit someone of a specific offence.

items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: After a lengthy trial, the case ended in acquittal.
items.note: The noun for being legally found not guilty; differs from pardon after conviction.

items.pt: arrepender-se; reconhecer o erro e desejar mudar
items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: Years later, he repented of the harm his actions had caused.
items.note: Repent of an action; refers to moral regret, sometimes associated with a change of behaviour.

items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The judge acknowledged his repentance but still imposed a custodial sentence.
items.note: Related to repent; expresses regret rather than a legal finding of innocence.

items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The head of state granted a pardon after new evidence raised doubts about the conviction.
items.note: An official act of forgiveness; does not mean the same as acquittal in a trial.

items.pt: um perdão oficial concedido após a morte
items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: Decades later, the government issued a posthumous pardon to the wrongly convicted activist.
items.note: Posthumous means granted or occurring after someone has died.

items.pt: isentar alguém de culpa; declarar alguém livre de responsabilidade
items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The independent inquiry exonerated the engineer from blame for the incident.
items.note: Formal: to clear someone from blame or responsibility; not necessarily a judicial acquittal.

items.pt: suspensão ou adiamento de uma punição; trégua temporária
items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The prisoner received a last-minute reprieve while the appeal was considered.
items.note: A temporary official delay or cancellation of punishment, not a finding of innocence.

items.pt: perdoar e deixar o passado para trás
items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: They agreed to forgive and forget after resolving the longstanding dispute.
items.note: Fixed order: forgive and forget, not forget and forgive.

items.word: apologise to a client for a mistake
items.pt: pedir desculpas a alguém por algo
items.section: B · Legal regret, responsibility and pardon
items.example: The project manager apologised to the client for missing the agreed deadline.
items.note: The person follows to; the offence follows for, often with an -ing clause.

items.example: After lengthy negotiations, the neighbouring states signed a peace treaty.
items.note: A written agreement between states intended to establish peace; more durable than a truce.

items.example: The opposing forces announced an armistice while diplomats discussed a permanent settlement.
items.note: An agreement to stop fighting during the process of negotiating peace.

items.example: The two groups agreed a truce so that aid could reach the isolated town.
items.note: A temporary cessation of hostility; may also describe disputes between individuals.

items.example: The new accord established a framework for scientific cooperation between the countries.
items.note: An official agreement, often between governments; not necessarily about warfare.

items.example: A ceasefire was announced to allow humanitarian workers into the affected region.
items.note: An agreement or order to stop shooting and fighting; can be temporary.

items.example: The rival organisations declared a truce ahead of the joint negotiations.
items.note: A common collocation for announcing a halt to hostilities.

items.example: The military delegations signed an armistice at the end of the summit.
items.note: Sign emphasises the formal agreement rather than the act of stopping combat itself.

items.pt: concordar com os termos de um acordo
items.example: Both parties agreed to the terms of the settlement after mediation.
items.note: A useful pattern for formal agreements; the preposition is to.

items.pt: um acordo é rompido; um entendimento fracassa
items.example: Observers feared the accord would collapse after the renewed border clashes.
items.note: Collapsing refers to an agreement ceasing to function or remain in force.
